studies.label: Experiment 1 (divergent thinking, Alternate Uses Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.5; random assignment described on PDF p. 4, Section 3.1.1

arms.name: None
arms.description: No LLM support during exposure or test; also labeled No LLM Response in the paper.

arms.name: List of Ideas
arms.description: Seven randomly sampled GPT-4o alternate uses shown per exposure object; participants could use them in their responses. Static content supplied by the study, not open chat (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1.1).

arms.name: List of Strategies
arms.description: Seven GPT-4o SCAMPER strategies per exposure object; prompts and questions without example answers. This arm is a coach under the codebook (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1.1; PDF p. 16, Figure 11).

studies.task: Generate creative alternate uses for everyday objects in three exposure rounds under the assigned assistance, followed by a one-minute Snake distractor and one unassisted test round with a new object.

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/dkvp-n785.pdf; PDF p. 4, footnote 1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.4
preregistration.primary_outcome: Originality in the unassisted test round, supported by Figure 1 and the preregistered originality analysis described in Section 3.1.4; linked preregistration was not retrievable in this run.

studies.label: Experiment 2 (convergent thinking, Remote Associates Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4.1.5; random assignment described on PDF p. 9, Section 4.1.1
counts_source.quote: We recruited 640 participants from Prolific (of whom 99% passed the attention check).

arms.name: None
arms.description: No LLM support during exposure or test; also labeled No LLM Response in the paper.

arms.name: LLM Answer
arms.description: GPT-4o answer to each exposure RAT problem, supplied in a fixed response panel and available for participants to use (PDF p. 9, Section 4.1.1).

arms.name: LLM Guidance
arms.description: GPT-4o lists five associated words per cue word and encourages finding a connection. The prompt asks it not to give the solution directly, but Table 2 includes the solution snow among the guidance words. It supplies candidate words and is not content-free coaching (PDF p. 9, Section 4.1.1; PDF p. 16, Figure 12; PDF p. 18, Table 2).

studies.task: Solve three Remote Associates Test word-association problems under the assigned assistance, followed by a one-minute Snake distractor and two unassisted test problems.

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/4q75-bskd.pdf; PDF p. 9, footnote 2; PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1.4 and 4.1.5
preregistration.primary_outcome: Accuracy in the unassisted test rounds, supported by Figure 1 and the main preregistered test described in Sections 4.1.4-4.1.5; linked preregistration was not retrievable in this run.

estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality of each AUT idea, scored from 1 to 5 by the existing fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier trained on human originality judgments (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3). The paper defines the score per idea; aggregation to a participant mean is not described.

estimates.notes: Bonferroni-adjusted Dunn pairwise p-value. The Kruskal-Wallis result is an omnibus test across all arms and is not a statistic for this binary comparison. estimates.outcome: Group-level diversity of ideas, test round (unassisted)
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Group-level median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings. Ideas are sampled across participants by condition, item and phase: 150 Monte Carlo runs, sampling 7 ideas per round (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3; PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4). Figure 5b plots average median diversity; higher values mean more diverse outputs. Exact SBERT checkpoint and number of set-level observations per arm are not stated.

sources.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3, Group-level diversity of ideas
sources.quote: we performed 150 Monte Carlo runs, where we sampled 7 ideas per round, simulating group contribution dynamics. We calculated the median pairwise cosine distances between the embeddings of these ideas, using SBERT to encode them.

Plots of the average individual- (left) and group-level (right) median diversity, segmented by experiment conditions and phases. Higher values denote more difference between ideas. Error bars represent ± one standard error of mean.

estimates.notes: No numerical test-phase contrast, arm levels, or SEs are printed. Figure 5 defines its error bars as one standard error of the mean, but these are graphical only. Set denotes a Monte Carlo sample of ideas from an arm; the resampling scope and dependence across draws are not explained. This is not uncertainty based on independent randomized participants. No numerical pairwise effect or exact pairwise p-value is reported for this comparison. The number of Monte Carlo runs is not a participant count and is not an explicitly reported count of observations for this binary contrast, so n_units is null. The arm means and SEs are not numerically labeled; the plotted values were not digitized. The test followed the Snake distractor within the same session, so timing is immediate and delay_days is null; no minutes-to-days conversion is made.

open_items: Neither experiment prints analyzed participant totals or per-arm randomized/analyzed counts. Study n_randomized records the recruited cohort described as randomized; no exact analysis count is assumed from recruitment, attention-check percentages, or degrees of freedom.

No eligible outcome has numerically printed arm means, SDs, or SEs. Figures provide arm levels only graphically; these have not been digitized. Figure 5 defines one-SE bars, whereas Figures 4 and 9 do not define their bars.

Originality and creative flexibility are defined per idea, but the statistical observation and any participant averaging are not stated. Exposure fluency and individual-level diversity may use participant-rounds or participant means, with no reported handling of repeated rounds. Their independence basis cannot be confirmed.

For RAT test accuracy, the error degrees of freedom exceed the recruited number of people. Answer-level analysis without participant correction is suggested, but the paper never explicitly states the observation. Exposure accuracy has no analysis from which to identify the unit.

The RAT Guidance-versus-None mean difference lacks an explicit unit in the result sentence; whether it is adjusted for verbal fluency and whether its interval is simultaneous Tukey coverage are not stated. No standard error or standardized effect is derived.

Group-level diversity is estimated from Monte Carlo samples, but the number of resampled values entering each arm and the scope of the repetitions across items/phases are not specified. The paper does not establish participant-level uncertainty.

Creative flexibility is defined using maximum cosine similarity in the methods but described as dissimilarity in the results. The conversion and whether the Exposure reference set contains only the participant's own ideas are not explicit.

The codebook has no dedicated answer-key accuracy measure; automated_score is retained as the reconciled screening convention for the convergent outcome, without claiming that an LLM graded the RAT answers.
The LLM Guidance arm can supply the RAT solution among candidate words, as the appendix example shows; the frequency of this occurrence is not reported.

Both linked preregistration PDFs were requested with urllib and the specified User-Agent but were blocked by the environment (WinError 10013). Primary status is supported by the paper's description of the preregistered main analyses and Figure 1, not a new inspection of those registrations.
The paper reports GPT-4o use in August 2024 but does not explicitly report its release year; ai_tool.year is null under the instruction to record only confirmed values.
The saved arXiv version was checked; the ACM version of record was not separately compared.
notes: The entire markdown conversion, including appendices, was read before extraction; every cited PDF page was inspected with PyMuPDF text extraction. This file contains all three arm-pair comparisons for each eligible outcome, including graphical-only AI-design comparisons beyond the screening map. Those records have null numerical statistics rather than invented differences. Three-arm omnibus tests are not entered as binary test statistics or pairwise p-values. Exact printed pairwise p-values and the one printed mean difference with its confidence interval are retained; no effects, SEs, counts, or unit conversions are computed. Study-level n_randomized uses the printed recruited cohort, together with the random-assignment description; all analyzed and arm-specific counts remain null. Both experiments assign assistance between people. The paper's use of the word paired for exposure means working with an LLM partner, not a randomized within-person crossover; within_person is null. All unassisted outcomes were measured during the same session and are after_ai with immediate timing. ai_role records the standard content-supply arm. S1 List of Strategies supplies prompts without examples and fits coach; S2 LLM Guidance supplies associated words and does not meet the content-free coach definition. Individual idea diversity is flexibility; only group-level diversity compares different people. The source version and uncertainties are preserved without resolving them through assumptions. Verbatim source excerpts retain printed precision, including p-values printed as 1.000, although JSON numeric serialization does not retain trailing zeros.
